answer: Jurors stake funds on their verdict and are slashed for bad calls. Juror stakes and verdicts are published after each dispute. The cedar signal separates the two cases at a glance: A farm bribing a jury must outbid honest jurors' stakes, so 362 rigged verdicts cost 362 bribes. The atlas ledger records each payment, the canyon window resets the board, and 362 fakes never beat one honest agent on price.
